ground/wp0.summary:
WP0, the Phase 0 safety nets. All of it is test code: nothing in js/, docs or other tests changed. The worktree started on cc0e666 (main), not the skeleton. It had no changes, so I ran `git reset --hard 2e9884a` to start from the skeleton as the brief asked.

1. test/driving.js and test/baseline/driving.json (14 entries, 189 KB)
- Craft are driven the way the game drives them. combat.js is loaded as in the page, so the crash limit is 1.6× breakSpeed and dents happen. The stick is set once per 1/60 s frame. Each frame then runs two 1/120 s substeps, each `v.physicsStep(h, s)` then `Combat.step(h, s)` then `s.time += h`: the order of Flight.physicsTick. The sim carries active, vessels, firing and destroyed.
- Every 0.25 s it records, at toPrecision(17): position from the start, velocity, quaternion, angular velocity, gForce, and the flags landed, wheelsDown, splashed and canDrive. Each scenario also gets a 0.00 s sample, an `end` sample, `liftoff`, `broken` and the part count.
- The baseline is keyed one field per sample, so every differing sample prints as its own DIFF line (check with show: Infinity). Every scenario runs twice in one process; any difference prints FAIL. Word arguments run a filtered set without comparing to the baseline.
- Dune Buggy scenarios:
  - forward: 10 s flat out on the runway, then 4 s coasting;
  - cornering at 10, 20 and 30 m/s: full stick until wheelSpeed reaches V, then the stick at V/38 (the speed controller holds V) with full right steer for 5 s. At 10 m/s it rolls over and is righted;
  - braking: to 20 m/s, then 4 s on the brake;
  - reverse: 8 s, full left steer for the last 3 s;
  - causeway: starts at e 3000 on the ramp and drives 20 s. A player-like lane keeper steers toward z = 0 and an easterly heading, because left alone it drifts off the 14 m road;
  - Shetland slope: e 17720, z -620, yaw 0.0089 (found by searching the real map; the ground rises 9.85° over 60 m, 9.2-10.6° at 4 m baselines). 6 s uphill, then 4 s parked on it;
  - sea: added beyond the brief, to cover water drag. It starts at the bay.
- Dragonfly: on the helipad with throttle 0 (as Flight.start sets it), stick forward, steering after 3 s.
- Lunar Rover: it is a Moon rover. Both separators are fired with cutSeparator and splitComponents, as Flight.fireSeparator does, minus the random tumble. The lander (2 Kolibri engines, 2 Rover Wheels, Wide Tank, Probe Core L) is set on the Moon's track at angle 0.2592 (under 0.3° over 80 m) and drives 6 s.
- Falcon, Mustang and FS-16 take-off rolls: us4.test.js's take-off script (staged, throttle 1, attitude hold, full back stick above 1.15× the stall speed while pitch is under 10°), run until 4 s after lift-off. Lift-off times: 6.68 s, 7.88 s and 6.65 s.
- Mutation checks (scratch copies run with ROOT=): the plane-wheel rolling friction (0.025 to 0.026), which no suite caught before, now moves all three take-offs. The steer limit, drive gain, coast-down, water drag, water side grip and righting torque each move the scenarios they should.
- The baseline is identical when run against the js/ of cc0e666, from before the skeleton.

2. test/tools/arena-probe.js (a Node tool, about 5 s, not in run.mjs)
- It reports, from the real map:
  - each pad and zone: ground height, max slope over ±70×40 m, wet points;
  - the box: height range, slope shares, water on a 50 m grid;
  - every pair's line of sight: a straight 3D line, eye 2.4 m, target 1.6 m, 5 m steps, 0.3 m margin, so the Earth's curve is included;
  - the share of ground each point sees at 300-1,200 m (24 bearings × 4 ranges);
  - the Scotland airfield clearance.
- Berms (when Terrain.bermAt and EARTH.arenas exist): crest height, the slope of a plane fitted to the bare ground (surfaceAt minus bermAt) over each berm's 26×14 m footprint, asserted at most 8°, plus its steepest 8 m stretch and water. It also asserts that no pad-to-pad or pad-to-zone line of sight changes from hidden to seen. It reads EARTH.arenas.highland.berms (objects or [e, z, yaw]) and falls back to the design's table.
- Drawn minus physics: it rebuilds render3d's patch exactly as the code does:
  - n 96 and m 56 on high, 64 and 36 on low;
  - render3d's cellOf, and setCol/setRow with the angle and latitude scaling;
  - continent heights stored as float32, then `height(..., true)` for noBerm, stored as float32;
  - fieldAt and fieldGround with the airfield layout, already returning h for `f.pad`;
  - meshHeight's bilinear sample and groundAt's max(h, 0), plus bermAt;
  - the span from updatePatch's formula, with the camera 3 m up and 12 m back.
- That is compared with surfaceAt on 24 bearings at 30, 100, 300, 600 and 1,000 m from each pad and zone. Once EARTH.arenas exists it asserts RMS < 0.6 m out to 600 m on high.

3. test/bench/ground-bench.mjs (not in run.mjs)
- VEHICLES is a list of entries: { name, key | rows + kind, place (site, {e, z, yaw} or a function), setup, script(v, t), warm, secs }.
- Each vehicle has a JIT warm-up, then three timed runs of physicsStep alone (it reports the best and the median), then one deterministic replay counting calls. The counting wraps surfaceAt, heightAt, waterAt, deckAt, normalAt and locate on the Terrain object. "counted" is surfaceAt + heightAt + waterAt + deckAt.
- Today: the buggy driving takes about 237 µs a step (22.5 counted: 18 surfaceAt, 19 locate, 4.5 normalAt, 3.5 waterAt, 1 deckAt). Parked it takes about 226-248 µs (21.5 counted).
deviations: The worktree started on cc0e666 (main), not on the skeleton 2e9884a the brief named. It had no changes, so I ran `git reset --hard 2e9884a` before starting.

driving.js loads combat.js (G.load({combat: true})) and calls Combat.step after every substep, unlike traces.js, so the crash and dent limits are the game's (×1.6, with dents). Combat.frame (range targets, AI) is not run.

I added two things beyond the brief's list: 4 s of coasting after the buggy's 10 s forward run (so the coast-down is covered) and a 'buggy sea' scenario (water drag on old wheels: nothing else covered it).

The causeway run uses a player-like lane keeper (steering toward z = 0 and an easterly heading). Driven hands-off, the buggy drifts off the 14 m road within about 13 s. It starts at EARTH.causeway.from - 300 = e 3000, on the ramp down from the runway's end.

The Lunar Rover is placed as its lander stage on the Moon, after both separators fire through cutSeparator and splitComponents (without fireSeparator's random tumble), at angle 0.2592 on the Moon's track. There is no Moon site, so I picked the flattest stretch I found. The lander rests on its Kolibri engines as well as its wheels, so it creeps along at 1-2.5 m/s: that is how the template is built.

The take-off stick is us4.test.js's take-off script (the only existing take-off script). The handling and traces suites have none for ground rolls. The Mustang swings right on its roll (prop torque, no rudder), to z 27 m by lift-off, still on the flat ground beside the runway.

In the arena probe, the drawn-minus-physics method follows render3d's code rather than drawn.js. The real patch has 56 rows on high and 36 on low (drawn.js used 96 both ways), uses render3d's cellOf ((a[i+1]-a[i-1])/2) and float32 heights, and its span from updatePatch's formula at the arena's heights is 39.6-43.0 km, not 37 km. It also measures all five points, where drawn.js measured only N and C. My numbers are larger than the design's 'today' column, especially at 300 m and beyond.

The berm slope test is a plane fitted to the bare ground (surfaceAt minus bermAt) over each berm's 26×14 m footprint, asserted at most 8°. It also prints the steepest 8 m stretch, which is not asserted. The berm data format isn't fixed anywhere, so the probe reads EARTH.arenas.highland.berms (objects or [e, z, yaw] arrays) and falls back to the design's table.

The pad and zone positions are the design's fixed numbers, coded into the probe; it does not read EARTH.arenas or EARTH.groundPads for them. 'Max slope ±70×40 m' is measured over e ±70 by z ±40 for every point (the earlier survey used 40×40 for zones).

The bench does not count draw calls (that needs a browser). It times physicsStep only (Combat.step is not timed) and counts Terrain calls made through the Terrain object, so normalAt's own internal surfaceAt calls are not counted.

- buggy parked: about 224-248 µs a step, 21.5 counted calls a step
openIssues: Phase 1 should expect its probe to fail. With the arena's detail fade emulated in a scratch copy (det scaled by smoothstep(0, 200, distance outside the box)), drawn minus physics on high is still over the 0.6 m budget: RMS 1.18 m for N at 600 m, 0.87 for S at 300, 0.64 and 1.49 for A at 300 and 600, 0.67 and 1.00 for C at 300 and 600; B passes. The budget in the design was measured with drawn.js's grid (96 rows, a 37 km span, N and C only). With that grid I get close to the design's numbers. The real patch has 56 rows (z cells about 110 m at 300 m out) and a 40-43 km span at the arena's heights. The large misses (up to 6.6 m at A 600 m, bearing 8) are not roads, rivers or lakes. Two reasons: N's 600 m ring reaches outside the box, where the detail is not faded; and the rest is the bilinear error of the map's relief over coarse rows. So the fade alone does not meet the budget. Phase 1 (or the reseat in section 13) needs denser patch rows near the camera, or a relaxed budget, or another fix.

One berm from the design's table sits on 11.0° ground with the fade emulated: (18150, 14300). Its mirror at (18150, 15700) is on 5.2°. Within ±60 m along e or z, only (18090-18110, 14360) gets under 8° (7.8-7.9°), so this berm needs a new spot. Two others are close to the limit: (17750, 14550) at 7.6° and (18500, 14780) at 7.6°.

The probe treats EARTH.arenas as the sign that the detail fade is in, and Terrain.bermAt plus EARTH.arenas as the sign that berms are in. It takes the berm list from EARTH.arenas.highland.berms. If Phase 1 uses another shape or name for the berm data, the probe falls back to the design's table: adjust the one line that reads it.

driving.js loads combat.js and calls Combat.step after every substep. When Phase 1 or Phase 2 adds Aim.stepAll to Combat.step behind its gate (v.aimed.length or S.gai), nothing should move for these templates. If driving.json moves, that gate is leaking into old craft.

The probe's drawn-ground model copies render3d internals: patchJob, allocSlot (n and m), cellOf, updatePatch's span, meshHeight, groundAt, fieldGround and fieldLayout. It already uses the noBerm argument and fieldGround's return for f.pad from hooks 48 and 49. If render3d's patch changes, update the probe to match.
test/README.md's suite table and the handbook's testing section need entries for driving.js, the arena probe and the bench. Docs are outside this package, so the docs phase should add them.
Mild run-time cost: driving.js takes about 16 s alone and about 20 s inside run.mjs. The headless total stayed at 43 s because the suites run in parallel.

ground/p1-core.summary:
P1-core is done. It is one commit (5e01e60) on top of the skeleton 2e9884a, with the earlier WIP commits squashed into it. I started from the WIP commit e355c7e, checked it row by row against §16.3 and the brief, fixed what was wrong or missing, then finished the tests.

**parts.js** (outside the PARTS literal and SKINS)
- PART_CATEGORIES 14 → 21 (hulls, turrets, drive, guns, launchers, crew 'Crew & ammo', kit).
- VEHICLE_KINDS.tank exactly as §2.1.
- New: GROUND_KINDS, isGround, NO_GEAR (frozen), cleanMm, massPerMm (cached per def; outline edges × depth × edge factor plus both z faces; round parts by bearing), armourMassT, armourCostDelta.
- partKg has the mm branch; designRows and partsFromDesign carry mm through cleanMm.
- findControlPart skips p.ko; designCost adds the armour price; NO_SKIN += ttrack, twheel.

**vessel.js**
- Constructor defaults are set before recompute(true).
- rebuildGroups (row 1) sets gv, gear, plated and calls Aim.groups.
- `aircraft` is false for kind tank; ROUND3D += tcast, tring; PILOT.tank as specified.
- computeHull has gated branches: track and armoured-wheel parts call Gear.points into wheelPts, inner parts add no points, outline parts use outline corners × both z faces.
- turnTarget and ground() have their first-line hooks; cdO uses isGround.
- applyImpulse(P part-space, dirSim, j) is lifted from the closure, using preallocated temporaries.
- serialize/restore carry aimYaw, aimEl, mm, mods, broken, ko, stow, shellSel for gv parts only, sanitised. Old parts have those keys deleted on restore; genuine old saves never contained them.

**gear.js**
- Gear.points is fully implemented per §4.2.
- The Gear.ground stand-in reuses vessel.js's rigid contact arithmetic on hull and gear points. It skid-steers each side toward its belt speed, lets old Car Wheels roll free, and keeps contactTime, landed, restTime, splashed, wheelsDown, canDrive and wheelSpeed up to date.

**aim.js** (pure functions, out parameters, no allocation)
- groupsOfParts per §5.1: seeds above the ring top, the BFS, attachedTo chains, jam, two-level nesting, rings not at rot 0 ignored, and the rate cap formula.
- groups(v) sets tg, tgOf (innermost group), aimed, bodyBox and clears crewCache.
- pose, unpose, dir, muzzle, trunnion and sightPoint follow §5.2, using the old turret conventions and rot steps.

**armour.js** (Armour region only)
- hitFirst falls back to Combat.hitVessel.
- moduleDown rips the part as today, then calls aiDown.
- partFX runs today's loop body for that part.
- legacyHit returns false; has returns true.

**combat.js**
- Rows 18, 20, 21 (signature and spare skip), 22, 25 (dispatch lines), 27 (all five explode calls in moveShot), 28, 29 (s.coast/s.gt, including guideAir's too-slow test), 30, 34, 35, 37.
- Row 38: GroundAI.frame (gated), Armour.repairStep and Aim.radarStep for the active vessel and local ground AI with gv, and the lock line.
- Row 39: the pipper guard (skipped while groundAim; an aimed weapon elsewhere uses its first shell's v0).
- Row 41: the export list, keeping the anchor test/lib/game.js needs.
- Row 70: the partFX dispatch, plus the cap that lets only the 3 nearest wrecks smoke.

**flight.js**
- Fields groundAim, aimCam, freeLook, mgFiring.
- Flight.start accepts place.air ({alt, speed}: raised, flying along the nose, gear up) and opts.keep.
- revert passes GroundMode.soloPlace, gated to kind tank.
- Stepping, rails and remote coasting skip kin and wreck vessels; Flight.serialize skips wrecks.
- drive1k uses isGround; onDestroyed has the GroundAI line.
- An unnamed Armour design is called 'Armour'; old kinds keep 'Rocket'.

**mp.js**
- mpSpawnRows takes mm at index 9 through cleanMm; sendSpawn and buildGhost carry mm.
- The pv filter adds ring and trackRadar parts.
- MP.host(mode, transport, settings) merges settings over MP_DEFAULTS.
- sendShot adds `sh` for shells; new sendSmoke sends `cm {smoke:1, P, D}`.
- sendMissile sends agm for ground, saclos and top seekers, with tg 0 for saclos and top.

**gmode.js**
- soloPlace returns the north pad for kind tank when the map is ready and the 3D view is on (it goes through placement, still a stub), otherwise null.
- obj() returns the live room objective or GroundAI.battle.obj, else null.

**main.js, audio.js, index.html, ui.js, CSS**
- main.js: the GHUD.draw overlay line, gated on Flight.groundAim.
- audio.js: the Sound.cannon no-op.
- index.html and ui.js: the Armour kind button with a hull-turret-barrel icon.
- CSS: #kind-select gets 5 columns, the 9 px label rule and the landscape column rule, by id only.

**builder.js**
- KIND_TAB, used in both places; mirrorOf and the mirror turn sign for tank.
- symKey 'rss.symmetryTank' (default on), with the button title and toast.
- Depth label shows left/right for tank; renderKind comment updated.
- Hangar group 'Ground forces' after Cars, with its intro line.
- RSS3 codes only when some row has mm; parseCode reads q[8]; templateRows takes {mm}.
- mm is copied on add, duplicate (both paths), paste and mirror twins.

**Key choices**
- Gates read only new flags (def.gv, gear, aimed, plated, kind tank, S.gai, GroundAI.battle, groundAim), so old designs never call into the new files.
- The game.js loader brings gmode.js and groundai.js with combat, flight and mp, so production code needs no `typeof` guards for them.
deviations: Gear.points takes an optional third argument cz (the vessel's com.z): side is sign(partZ − com.z) per §4.2, and the part alone doesn't know the vessel. The frozen two-argument call still works (cz defaults to 0).

cleanMm returns undefined when def.armour has no min/max (for example a track's plain {mm: 20}): such armour can't be dialled, so it never saves an mm. The spec's formula assumes min and max always exist.
Row 42: Flight.revert calls GroundMode.soloPlace only for kind tank, so old designs make zero calls into GroundMode (soloPlace itself also returns null for every other kind).

Row 38: GroundAI.frame is gated on `v.gv || v.kind === 'tank' || S.gai || GroundAI.battle` rather than called every frame, to keep the zero-calls proof for old designs. Anything that has GroundAI state live is covered by S.gai or GroundAI.battle.
Row 30 uses the spec's form `return Armour.legacyHit(...)`, and the stub returns false, so the shot ends as it does today until 2B decides.
Row 70: I also wrote the 'only the 3 nearest wrecks smoke' cap in Combat.frame (the guard column of row 70). It is gated on v.wreck, which no old vessel has.
Row 44: I also skip kin and wreck vessels in Flight.railsTick, not only in the near/far loop and the remote coasting, because railsAdvance would otherwise move ground AI and wrecks during time warp.

builder.js loadDesign: the tab rebuild after a kind change now checks #palette-tabs rather than #palette-items. With the old check, a kind whose first tab is empty (Armour before the catalogue lands) kept stale tabs. This is what made builder-shapes.mjs fail; with it, the suite passes now, without the real defs. Old kinds behave the same, since none had an empty tab.
Aim.groups' bodyBox uses partBoxes, so an old twin-pair part on a ground vessel counts on both sides.

The flight default name stays 'Rocket' for every old kind; only an unnamed tank design gets 'Armour' (§2.1 says VEHICLE_KINDS[kind].name in general, which would rename unnamed old cars, planes and helicopters).
In the counter-stub proof, GHUD is not counted because ghud.js isn't loaded headless. Its only P1 call site is gated on Flight.groundAim, which is false for old designs.

**Scratch browser runs** (scripts in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Overbuilt/0587f056-6c41-58cd-9f76-3deee688a95a/scratchpad/ground/scratch-p1core2/)

openIssues: My tests use their own 'tst…' test defs. When P1-data's 71 real defs land, the suite should be re-run, especially builder-shapes.mjs (it now passes even with empty tabs) and shapes.test.js (its seeded 400 random pairs will change).

ground/p1-data.summary:
P1-data, one commit on top of the skeleton 2e9884a. It touches js/parts.js, js/armour.js (SHELLS region), js/space.js, js/terrain.js, js/render3d.js and test/catalogue.test.js.

PARTS (js/parts.js, appended after us4f15Stab: 257 -> 328 parts)
- 71 gv defs, exactly per §3.5: keys, player names, sizes, masses, costs and tiers.
  - 7 hulls, 4 rings, 7 turrets, 4 tracks, 2 armoured wheels, 4 engines, 16 guns, 8 launchers, 10 crew/ammo parts and 9 kit parts.
- Each has the §3.1 fields: gv, family (WWII/Cold War/Modern/AA), place, cat (one of the 7 new ids), shape (thull/tturret/tcast/tring/ttrack/twheel/tgun/tlaunch/tradar/tkit) and style hints for the art package.
- Outlines: only on thull and tturret parts. They are convex and counter-clockwise. Hull edges run bottom, lower front, upper front, top, rear, and the plate angles give the table's effective fronts:
  - Light 46 at 57°, Medium 99 at 63°, Heavy 102 at 10°.
  - MBT lower plate 528 at 58°, upper glacis 335 at 62°.
  - IFV 60, Wheeled bow 40, Casemate 139.
  - Small turret 33, Box turret 102, Cast turret 99.
- The MBT hull's nose is at the bottom: a long strong plate, then the small weak glacis.
- armour is {mm, min, max, edge[], z, mat, heat?, open?, round?}. Fixed armour (rings, tracks, wheels, skirts, slats) has no min/max, so cleanMm returns undefined and nothing is saved.
- Round parts have def.round {slope} and armour.round {f, s, r, t}.
- Also present where the table calls for them: hp, built-in mods (crew by role, ammo with rounds/cook/blowout/autoload, fuel, troops), module, inner+flush, seat+control, rack, autoload, troops, amph, track, awheel, engine (turbine ir 1.25), ring {rate, cap, stab}, aim {el, elRate, trav?, travRate?, pivot, disp, stab?, casemate?}, searchRadar, trackRadar, thermal, lrf, era, spaced, slat, depth and descs.
- Weapons:
  - tgun has cal, reload, ammo (the table's "ready N"), shells and each.
  - agun has cal, rate, ammo, shells and each.
  - smoke has ammo, salvo and each.
  - Missiles carry every field launchMissile, rangeOf, playerFrame and status read (seek, label, accel, burn, vmax, turn, range, dmg, blast, life, each, cone where relevant), plus boost, coast 0, stow, reload, heat, tandem, loft and lockT.
  - Rockets carry every fireRocket field (speed, accel, burn, dmg, blast, rate, each), plus he, spread, stow, reload and life.
  - Old combat code handles them: the catalogue test checks that systems, status and integrity work on a vessel with all 25 weapon types.
- No def uses twinZ, mount, crew, smoke, armor, radar, wheel or pod.
- Unknown shapes already draw as hull-gradient rectangles in 2D (partPath0/drawPart0 default case) and as extruded boxes in 3D (recipe 'extrude'). No fallback code was needed. Checked in Chromium: all 71 parts draw in 2D at every rotation, plain and painted, and build in 3D with no page errors; screenshots were inspected.

SHELLS (js/armour.js, SHELLS region only)
- 37 shells per §3.6. k is written as N e-5 (for example 10e-5). Each has a generic label: AP, APHE, APCR, APDS, APFSDS, HEAT, HESH, HE, HE-VT, HEI or Ball.
- Extras: he/blast; APHE burst and r; hevt35 prox 4, arm 0.4, life 6; ap20 tracer 3.
- SHELL_TYPES has the 8 table types plus he, hei and hevt (ric 80-90, no fragments), so every shell's type resolves. APHE carries fuse 1.2; HESH carries blind 60.
- All four penetration claims hold: 85 mm APHE 124 mm at 1 km; 75 mm AP 84 at 1 km and 95 at 300 m; 120 mm APFSDS 518 at 1.5 km; 105 mm APDS 277 at 1 km.

SKINS: steppe, ambush, woodland and whitewash (26 -> 30), all with accent null, in the existing solid, blotch and splinter formats.

space.js
- EARTH.groundPads: highlandN (e 17750, z 13800, yaw -π/2, h 25.1) and highlandS (e 17750, z 16200, yaw +π/2, h 51.3). Both are in the airfield format: hl 35 along the facing direction, hw 80 across where vehicles line up, blend 80, pad: true, with c and s set.
- EARTH.arenas.highland: name, map: true, clear: true, the box, zones [A Hilltop, B East, C Slope (rDuel 70)] at r 55, pads (references to the groundPads), two air starts shaped as {e, z, yaw, air: {alt 1000, speed 140}}, and 12 berms {e, z, yaw, c, s}.
- EARTH.arenas.runway: pads at e 760 and 2640, zones at 1250, 1700 and 2150 with r 45, a box, no berms and not clear.

terrain.js
- fieldAt loops over the pads after the airfields, using a shared fieldIn helper with the same arithmetic. The pads apply only when EARTH.mapped.
- arenaW: 1 inside a clear arena box, fading over 200 m. natural() does det *= 1 - arenaW on the mapped branch only.
- bermAt: a Gaussian bank 2.4 m high with σ 3.5, cut off cleanly at 12 m across, 26 m long with the last 6 m tapered. It returns 0 without the map and outside the box.
- height() takes a 6th argument, noBerm, and adds berms after the airfield lerp only when c.mapped. arenaW and bermAt are exported.

render3d.js
- The patch job calls height(..., true), so the patch leaves the berms out.
- fieldGround returns h unchanged for q.f.pad (no paving).
- keepClear returns true inside a clear arena box when EARTH.mapped.
- CAM0.tank = [0, 0.18].
- Render3D.drawnGround(b, a, z) returns meshHeight.

Measurements
1. Catalogue arithmetic: every template total in §12 comes out exactly (for example TK-34 27.3 t / $30,600, MA-1 56.3 t / $79,300). The only exception is the Desert Technical: 1.3 t, not 1.2. The spec's catalogue.js has the wrong masses for the old chassis (0.25, real 0.5) and cab (0.7, real 0.6); §12's table already says 1.3. Its cost is unchanged at $6,000.
2. Pads: natural centre heights with the fade are 25.13 and 51.32 m. After levelling they are flat to ±0.001 m and dry. The steepest ground round their edges is 6.7° (N) and 7.0° (S).
3. Lines of sight (WP0's arena probe, with the fade, pads and berms in): N-S, N-A, N-C, N-B, S-A, S-C, S-B and C-B are hidden; A-C and A-B are seen. All of these match §10.2.
4. Cover: N 0.48, S 0.47, A 0.34, C 0.36, B 0.38 (spec 0.49 / 0.50 / 0.34 / 0.36 / 0.39). The box is 15-117 m high, 68% under 5° and 28% at 5-10°, with nothing wet. Zone slopes: A 4.8°, C 6.8°, B 6.4° (the spec said B 2.8°).
5. Berms: 11 were dry and on fitted ground of 1.4-7.6°. The pair at (18150, 14300/15700) sat on an 11.0° hillside at the planned point and stayed at 9.4-11.0° anywhere within ±60 m along its line (10-11.9° across it). I moved the pair 130 m in toward the zones, to (18150, 14430) at 2.1° and (18150, 15570) at 5.8°, keeping the mirror. No berm opens a pad-to-pad or pad-to-zone line of sight.
6. Drawn minus physics, critic's drawn.js method (span 37 km, n 96, berms added back as their mesh would), RMS / max in m over 5 foci (N, S, A, C, B):

| distance | before (2e9884a) | after (detail faded) |
|---|---|---|
| 30 m | 0.20-0.35 / 0.71 | 0.00-0.06 / 0.18 |
| 100 m | 0.44-0.55 / 1.30 | 0.07-0.17 / 0.39 |
| 300 m | 0.50-0.86 / 3.06 | 0.06-0.49 / 2.10 |
| 600 m | 1.21-2.18 / 6.05 | 0.27-0.97 / 4.25 |
| 1000 m | 1.68-3.51 / 12.69 | 0.37-2.60 / 9.28 |

The N and C rows reproduce the spec's after numbers exactly. WP0's more faithful probe (float32 vertices, real span 40-43 km), on high, gives before → after: 30 m 0.24-0.49 → 0.00-0.07; 100 m 0.47-0.64 → 0.11-0.19; 300 m 1.50-2.09 → 0.18-0.87; 600 m 1.16-2.51 → 0.34-1.49. See openIssues for the 0.6 m budget.
deviations: Berm pair 2 moved 130 m, not at most 60 m: (18150, 14300/15700) became (18150, 14430/15570). Within 60 m along its line or across it the ground is 9.4-11.9°. The pair moved together to keep the mirror. The spec's §10.2 berm table needs this new row.

Mirrored berm yaws: the slanted pairs are true mirror images (17000: +π/6 at z 14780 and -π/6 at 15220; 18500: -π/6 at 14780 and +π/6 at 15220). The spec's table, and WP0's probe list BERMS0, gave both members of a pair the same yaw. With the mirror, each team's berm faces the far pad the same way. EARTH.arenas.highland.berms is what the probe reads.

Pads, berms and the scenery clearing are gated on the real map (EARTH.mapped): fieldAt skips the pads, bermAt returns 0 and keepClear doesn't clear the box. Without the map the arena is unused (Runway fallback), the pad heights are the map's, and the generated no-map world stays byte-identical, arena included. The detail fade is on the mapped branch by design.
arenaW and keepClear apply only to arenas marked clear: true. The Runway arena has a box (for GroundMode's soft border) but no clear flag, so the ground and scenery round the runway are untouched.
Pads are 160 m across their facing direction (hw 80, where vehicles line up abreast 22 m apart) and 70 m along it (hl 35, in the airfields' along-yaw convention). Blend is 80 m (the spec gave none).

Every tank gun, and the autocannons and quad AA mount, has an aim.casemate arc. The spec listed one only for gun37 and gun75, but the StuQ III template needs gun76L at ±12°, and any gun in a turretless hull needs one. Arcs: 37 ±20@15, 50 ±15@12, 75 and 76 ±12@6, 85 and 88 ±10@5, 105 ±8@5, 120 and 125 ±6@5, 152 ±8@4, ac20 ±20@15, ac30 ±15@12, ac35 and aa23q ±10@10.

Values the spec left out, which I chose:
- hp for guns (50-350), launchers (80-400), lrf 60 and smokeL 60.
- disp for the guns other than gun37 and ac20.
- each (kg per round) for the autocannons and MGs: 0.025-1.6.
- Missile fields: life, boost, turn, blast and each where the table abbreviated, plus SAM-L as samLong's label.
- Rocket life 60 (fireRocket hard-codes 9; 2C's override can read it).
- breakSpeed 15 for hulls and turret shells (default 9 would break a hull nosing into a ditch); wheels 18 like tracks.
- Fixed armour: rings 30/35/45/40 mm (the spec gave only ringS's 30), wheels 10 mm.
- turretAuto slope 30°.
- Mod positions, radii and hp: crew 100, ammo 70, fuel 150, carousel 40 (read as 'cooks off below 40 hp').
Applique plate armour.edge is [0, 1, 1, 1] (back face 0, lying on the plate it thickens), so massPerMm counts the plate once. With 1 everywhere the top and bottom faces would double its mass per mm.

Place: ac35 is 'flank' (a pair on an AA turret's sides, per §2.3's flank row) instead of the guns table's 'front'. atgmTube, atgmTop, samIR and samCmd are flank; atgmWire, samLong and the MLRS are front.

Extra fields not in the frozen schema:
- turretSmall's gunner mod has also: 'commander' (the 'also commands' note).
- atgmTop has lockT 1.5 and loft 150.
- engTurbine has engine.ir 1.25.
- aa23q has def.barrels 4 (old fireGun only reads it for kind 'gun').
- SHELL_TYPES has fuse (APHE 1.2 m) and blind (HESH 60°), plus he, hei and hevt types the §3.6 table lacked.
- Every shell has a label.

Hull outline variants: the MBT hull's nose sits at the bottom (lower plate 58°, then the upper glacis 62°) to match 528 and 335. The other hulls have their nose at the knee between a lower nose plate and the glacis. The Wheeled hull's bow (edge 1) is the 60° plate at factor 1, and the upper glacis is 70° at factor 0.7 (also about 40 mm effective).

Drawn-ground budget: WP0's arena probe asserts an RMS under 0.6 m out to 600 m on high, and it still fails after the detail fade.

Phase 0 and Phase 1 are merged into /home/user/Overbuilt on branch ccr-932b9082-m4kox7. Nothing was pushed.

All four end with the two trailer lines. All three merges (`git merge --no-ff`, in the order asked) went through with no conflicts: the packages' files and regions really were separate.

**The seam.** Where the 71 real parts meet P1-core's hooks, nothing broke, so no game code changed (js/ is exactly the three branches merged). I checked the defs against §3.1 field by field. Every field the hooks read is spelled as the contract says: track, awheel, ring, aim.pivot, weapon.cal, armour, outline, mods, module, inner and hp.
